chunks: And ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh and others narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbār, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Uthmān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Hilāl, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: The heavens wept over al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) and Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (peace be upon him), and they did not weep over anyone other than them. I asked: ‘How did they weep?’ He said: ‘It remained for forty days, rising like the sun with redness and setting with redness.’ I asked: ‘Is that its weeping?’ He said: ‘Yes.’
ai.seo_question: How did the heavens weep for Imam al-Husayn and Yahya ibn Zakariyya according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) narration that the heavens wept for al-Husayn (a.s.) and Yahya ibn Zakariyya (a.s.), manifesting this cosmic grief by remaining red for forty days at sunrise and sunset. This unique phenomenon distinguishes their martyrdoms from all others, emphasizing the profound impact of their sacrifices on the natural world. The redness of the sky serves as a perpetual sign of divine sorrow, linking the Ahl al-Bayt’s suffering to the broader narrative of prophetic martyrdom.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh and others narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdil Jabbār, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faďďāl, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Uthmān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Hilāl, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: The heavens wept over Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) and Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (a.s.) and they have never wept over anyone other than them. I asked, “How did the heavens weep?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “The heavens became red for forty days like the sun at the time of sunrise and sunset.” I asked, “Is that how the heavens weep?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes.”
